thread:
Nina: FYI: we're changing the default request ID behavior across SDKs and the hosted API. Starting next month we will require a client-supplied idempotency/request header (x-redwood-request-id) for all mutating generate calls. This improves tracing and deduplication for retries.

Rafi: Docs summary: new header "x-redwood-request-id" (RFC4122 UUID recommended). We'll add a short migration doc, code snippets for py/js/go, and a note about server-side fallback generation.

Omar: Platform note: hosted API will accept requests without the header for 30 days while we warn in responses. After the grace period missing headers will get 400 unless the SDKs generate them. Dedicated/private installs can opt to enforce immediately via config.

Leah: Support playbook: if customers see 400s after enforcement, ask whether they're on an old SDK or using a proxy that strips headers. Provide the patch snippet.

Nina: SDK changes: py/js/go will auto-generate a stable uuid per request if the caller doesn't supply one, but we will flip to emitting a warning header that indicates SDK-generated ids during grace. We'll bump minor semver and call out the behavior. Example (py):
```python
resp = client.generate(prompt, request_id="3f8a...-uuid")
```
or SDK will set client.request_id = uuid4() if not provided.

Omar: Rollout timeline:
- Day 0: announce + docs draft.
- Day 7: SDK releases with auto-gen behavior and deprecation warnings.
- Day 37: hosted API enforcement begins (400 on missing header).

Rafi: I'll add a troubleshooting section: common causes (HTTP clients/proxies dropping headers, load balancers rewriting, old SDKs), and a small header-echo test endpoint that returns the request-id for verification.

Leah: Also add a support snippet to detect duplicated responses due to retry logic: look for same request-id with different outcome.

ci-bot: CI: SDK minor releases created (py-js-go) and docs PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/780
